chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: Climbing the levels of New Orleans bands
summary: Danny explains that a young musician moved up grade by grade between bands, hearing relatives' gossip about who was who.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Slow Drag. (?) Joe. See, you know... Like, I'm from New Orleans, and I will give credit where it's due. You know, a lot of these people what you think... You had levels. Like, when I started playing here, you went with this little jive band. You went to the first grade. Then you went Primer or Kindergarten. Then you jumped up here to this band. Then you went to that first grade, then you went in the second grade, third grade and the fourth grade. When you'd get somebody like Lee Collins, who was playing funky with a band, or David Jones, them people would be playing.

Well, you got all these relatives, see, and they're telling you who is who. Who is on first base and who ain't, who to work with, and who would be beat somebody out of money, and who was the bandleader who is crooked -- and you'd hear all kinds of intrigue of the business. You know, like I'm listening and listening, but I like it, because you're somebody. You sit on a sideline, nobody know you. If you're a longshoreman, or you're a plasterer, you're a (?), whatever.
